deliverable: Independent output-column shard variant of the single MixedKernel. Each program computes the COMPLETE softmax for its query rows and writes only its disjoint output columns; there is no cross-program merge, no GM probability matrix and no second kernel. A logical (batch, kv-head, query, column-shard) job is mapped to the 1D bx grid for BSND and BNSD.

sharded_equivalence.statement: sharded output is BIT-IDENTICAL to the unsharded variant, which is the expected result: a shard repeats QK and softmax but only partitions the PV output columns, so no arithmetic changes. Measured, not argued.

unsharded_regression.comparator: original cannbench_contract.Harness + npu_compare.compare_case_result, original thresholds, warm fp64 oracle cache
unsharded_regression.note: re-run AFTER the sharding change, so the 20/20 in G60 is not being inherited on trust

job_mapping.program: (batch b, KV head h, query-row tile r0, output-column shard d0)
job_mapping.grid: 1D bx; the column-shard axis is LEAST significant so shards of one row tile are adjacent programs and reach the same K tiles together
job_mapping.bsnd: r = i*G + g, so i = r//G and g = r%G
job_mapping.bnsd: r = g*S + i, so g = r//S and i = r%S
job_mapping.why_this_matters: r is a programming row index, NOT a query position. The two layouts agree only at G == 1, so a GQA shape is the only thing that distinguishes a correct mapping from using r directly.

cost_model.meaning: sharding trades duplicated QK/softmax/K-read work for occupancy. It is not a free win and is only worth it when occupancy, not arithmetic, is binding.

guard.condition: shard_count must divide the PV panel count
guard.why: the shard index varies at RUNTIME inside the job loop, so the per-shard panel count must be a compile-time constant and equal across shards; an uneven split would need runtime loop bounds. D_nope=448 has 7 panels of 64, so it admits 1 and 7 but NOT 2 or 4 -- refused loudly rather than padded.

my_own_test_bugs_recorded: A device run appeared to fail with 'device_type mismatch' and I initially suspected my sharding change. It was my harness: g60_one.py passed the CPU tensors to the reference kernel instead of the NPU tensors. The reference runs on device. My kernel had succeeded; the traceback came from the reference call on the line after it. Fixed by passing the device tensors to the reference and keeping the golden on CPU.
This is the third time a failure in MY harness has looked like a kernel defect. The pattern is consistent: the harness is less scrutinised than the kernel, so its bugs are attributed to the kernel.
not_claimed: No claim that sharding is FASTER. The cost model predicts the regime in which it can help; no cycle timings were taken and no shard count is recommended on performance grounds. Per cases/mla.md 6.2 and 9, the choice must be made by measurement, and that measurement is deferred to the performance search rather than invented here.
The per-shard QK repeat is stated as a multiplier, not as a measured time.
Uneven shard widths are not supported by design and their feasibility is not assessed.
